title: Flip Columns For Maximum Number of Equal Rows
summary: Given an m x n binary matrix, select any number of columns to flip all cells within them.
statement: Given an m x n binary matrix, select any number of columns to flip all cells within them. Determine the greatest number of rows that can have all cells equal after performing any number of flips.
constraints: One operation flips every value in a chosen column.
Return the maximum number of rows that can become internally constant after the same flips.
hints: A row becomes constant under a flip mask determined up to complement by its first bit.
Normalize each row by XOR with its first value.
Rows with the same normalized tuple can all become constant together; return the largest frequency.
Equal normalized patterns mean rows are identical or complements in exactly the required columnwise way.
editorial: Equal normalized patterns mean rows are identical or complements in exactly the required columnwise way.

tests.explanation: No flip choice makes both rows constant, so the maximum is one.
The rows are complements and one column flip makes both constant.
